title: Supplier Collapse
briefing: Corvane Materials has entered administration. Liner deliveries have stopped. Valtren has 11 days of stock.

evidence.title: Stock
evidence.body: 11 days of liners at current use. Pharma uses 40% of them.

evidence.title: Alternatives
evidence.body: Fennick Packaging: 8 weeks to qualify for pharma, can supply food-grade in 5 days at +9%. Two overseas suppliers: 4-6 weeks' shipping.

evidence.title: Administrator
evidence.body: Corvane's administrator may sell remaining stock to the highest bidder.

questions.prompt: How do you allocate the 11 days of liners?

options.label: Reserve liners for pharma, switch food loads to Fennick food-grade liners within 5 days, and bid for Corvane's stock
options.feedback: Protects the strictest contracts while alternatives come in.

options.label: Keep normal allocation so no client is singled out, while Procurement searches the market for replacement supply
options.feedback: Pharma runs out in 11 days with no alternative qualified.

options.label: Suspend food deliveries so every remaining liner goes to pharma until supply is restored

questions.prompt: How do you shorten Fennick's 8-week pharma qualification?

options.label: Work with the pharma clients' quality teams on an expedited, risk-based qualification with extra monitoring
options.feedback: Clients share the problem; involve them.

options.label: Use Fennick's food-grade liners on pharma loads now and complete the qualification paperwork in parallel
Run the full 8-week qualification and source overseas stock to bridge the gap

questions.prompt: What do you tell pharma clients?

options.label: Tell them now: the situation, stock cover, the plan, and ask for help with qualification
Wait until the supply plan is firm, so clients hear a solution rather than a problem
options.feedback: They will find out from the news.

options.label: Explain that Corvane's failure is outside Valtren's control and that alternatives are being sought
options.feedback: True, but they chose Valtren, not Corvane.

options.label: Supplier tiering with credit monitoring and pre-qualified second sources for every tier-1 input
options.feedback: A standing control for the next one.

options.label: Require Procurement to justify every single-source contract to the executive committee in future
options.feedback: The exclusive deal was a risk decision, not just a procurement one.

options.label: Treat it as a rare event: supplier insolvency at this scale happens once in a decade

lesson: Supplier failure is a stock, time and priority problem. Protect the strictest commitments, involve clients early, and build second sources before you need them.

escalation.text: Nobody from risk picked up "Supplier Collapse" in time. The executive team handled it alone, late and without a plan, and the damage spread.
